finding.summary: This authenticated project-member endpoint executes SELECT * on sf_releases and returns r.files directly without database-side count/content/encoded-metadata bounds. A privileged database corruption/direct mutation that replaces files with an extremely large JSONB array or unknown nested extension metadata is fully decoded into Node and serialized to the caller. This is a retained-payload allocation/response-size exposure on a separate raw-detail read. It is distinct from the four T26 mutation/evidence readers; no unauthorized cross-project read was observed because the authenticate prehandler resolves and checks project membership.
finding.recommended_followup: Register a separate bounded retained-release detail-read hardening increment after T26: use a scoped row lock and the reusable PostgreSQL scalar preflight before selecting files, retain the existing successful response shape for bounded valid historical records, and return a fixed existing-style unavailable response for corrupt/over-budget rows. Keep authorization and archived read behavior intact.
finding.scope_note: Do not treat T26 four-route closure as all retained reads closed. This is a privileged corruption resource-exhaustion condition, not evidence of routine-row exploit or a new credential/data-confidentiality breach.
finding.limitations: Static preliminary review only; no tests/builds/scans/lifecycle run. Not exact-head approval.
